analysis.method: Archive-wide keyword retrieval followed by inspection of high-signal assistant music outputs and immediate user reactions/corrections.

positive_patterns: Strong section architecture: intro, verse, hook, bridge or release when the song benefits from it.
Hooks work best as catch zones supported by setup/anchor lines and followed by a release or continuation.
Dense passages benefit from internal and multisyllabic rhyme while remaining one coherent human-flowing thought.
Dynamic line length matters: short impact lines mixed with longer connected runs create cadence instead of uniform walls of text.
Callbacks, double meanings, concrete imagery, punchlines, adlibs and controlled repetition create identity and replay value.
Beat-aware rewrites should change cadence, pauses and line length rather than merely swapping vocabulary.
The finished lyric should hide its construction mechanics unless annotation is requested.
Developed main verses should usually be long enough to establish, evolve, and pay off an idea; default toward substantial verses unless the user asks for brevity.
Bridges can use recognizable repetition as structural glue, with later repetitions optionally morphing a line, ending, image, response, or cadence rather than becoming a completely unrelated section.
negative_patterns: Generic filler used only to complete a rhyme.
Overusing the same motif or adjective until the track sounds templated.
Excessive section labels or production commentary inside the lyric.
Uniform four-line symmetry across every section.
Confusing retrieval of an existing song with permission to invent source lyrics.
Searching literal deictic placeholders such as 'that song' instead of resolving the prior song entity.

generation_contract.creative_mode: Original writing is allowed only when the user is asking to create, rewrite, remix, freestyle, extend, or transform original material.
generation_contract.retrieval_mode: When the user asks for existing lyrics or source text, resolve the song title and artist from recent context and retrieve/verify rather than creatively completing missing material.
composition_priorities: human variation in line length and syntax

default_song_shape.verse_length: Default to substantial, developed verses rather than short verse stubs. Unless the user asks for short/compact writing or the musical form clearly calls for brevity, aim for roughly 12–20 performance lines per main verse, with enough room for setup, development, rhyme-chain evolution, callbacks, and payoff.
default_song_shape.verse_rule: Do not confuse dense writing with short writing. A strong verse should develop an idea across multiple bars and vary line length/cadence instead of ending as soon as one rhyme chain lands.
default_song_shape.bridge_behavior: Bridges are normally shorter than verses and may repeat a memorable phrase or melodic/rhythmic anchor. On later bridge passes, repetition may stay exact or morph slightly—changed ending, added response line, altered image, intensified wording, or cadence shift—while remaining recognizably the same bridge.
default_song_shape.chorus_behavior: Hooks/choruses may repeat more strongly than verses; purposeful repetition is desirable when it creates catch and identity. Repeated hooks can receive small final-pass variations when useful.
default_song_shape.exceptions: Follow explicit user length/structure requests over these defaults. Very fast BPM, call-and-response, minimalist genres, intros/outros, or intentionally sparse songs may justify shorter sections.
